statement: Paper C Lemma 8.2 (Chernoff), exact form. A word w of length d is L-bad if o_t(w) log_2 3 − t > −L for every 1 ≤ t ≤ d (LBad). For C ≥ 5, p_C = (1 − 1/C)/log_2 3, e(C) = C D(p_C‖1/2)/log 2, and every d ≥ 1 with d ≥ C L: #{L-bad words of length d} ≤ 2^d · 2^{−e(C) L} (LBad_count_le). Engine: the constant weight has weightGen (1+x)^d (weightGen_one), so the Markov tilt weight_markov of RateFreeDensity gives #{o(w) ≥ k} ≤ (1+x)^d/x^k for x ≥ 1 (count_oddCount_ge_le), hence #{o(w) ≥ p d} ≤ (1+x)^d/x^{pd} with a real exponent (count_oddCount_ge_real_le); at x = p/(1−p) this is exp(d h(p)) with h the binary entropy (tilt_value, count_oddCount_ge_le_exp), i.e. 2^d exp(−d D(p‖1/2)) (count_oddCount_ge_le_kl); D(p‖1/2) ≥ 0 by log x ≤ x − 1 (klHalf_nonneg); an L-bad word has o_d ≥ p_C d when d ≥ CL (LBad_oddCount_ge); and 1/2 ≤ p_C < 1 for C ≥ 5 from 3^5 ≤ 2^8 (logb_two_three_le, half_le_pC, pC_lt_one). Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. The O-rooted statement with ε and L_0 is not formalized. A count of words, not a statement about Juggler starts.

Paper C Corollary 5.5 (fate contagion) at every 0 < lambda <= 100/203, each clause in its log-mass form and its dyadic-block form, as named theorems: (1) the reach-one class R, backward-closed and containing 1, has sum_{n in R, n <= x} 1/n >= K (log x)^lambda for x >= x_0 (Density.reachesOne_logMass_averaged) and natural density >= c (log y)^(lambda-1) on a dyadic block inside every large shell (reachesOne_natDensity_averaged); (2) if some start fails, the failures have the same bounds (Production.failures_logMass_averaged, Density.failures_natDensity_averaged); (3) the basin of any state m >= 1, the starts whose orbit passes through m, has them (basin_logMass_averaged, basin_natDensity_averaged) -- the paper's clause is the case of a periodic m, the basin of that cycle -- and so do the divergent starts if some orbit diverges (escapes_logMass_averaged, escapes_natDensity_averaged). Paper C Corollary 5.4 (natural density, infinitely often): the dyadic pigeonhole, from a shell bound. If K (log X)^lambda <= sum_{sqrt X < n <= X, n in A} 1/n with 0 < lambda <= 1, K > 0 and X >= 3, then some y with sqrt X < y <= X has #(A cap (y/2, y]) >= (K/12) y (log y)^(lambda-1) (Density.exists_block_of_shell; the block is Ioc (y/2) y in the natural numbers, blockCount). PROOF, the manuscript's: the shell (sqrt X, X] is covered by the blocks (X/2^(j+1), X/2^j] for j <= log_2 X, at most 3 log X of them since log 2 > 1/2 (halfLogMass_le_blocks, through Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to on j = floor(log_2(X/n)), block_index); a block's log-mass is at most 2 #/y because every member exceeds y/2 (block_logMass_le); the best block is at least the average (Finset.exists_le_of_sum_le); and y^2 > X gives log y > (log X)/2, which with lambda - 1 < 0 turns (log X)^(lambda-1) into (log y)^(lambda-1) at the cost of 2^(1-lambda) <= 2. From g_A(t) >= K t^lambda for t >= t_1 this is Corollary 5.4 with c = K/12 for every X >= ceil(e^t_1) + 3 (natDensity_of_shell_bound), and with Theorem 5.18 (Production.contagion_averaged at eta_0 = 10^-5) it holds for every 0 < lambda <= 100/203 with no hypothesis (natDensity_averaged). Kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. The blocks found are distinct as X runs through the powers of 4, so there are infinitely many; no bound on every block is claimed, the range 100/203 < lambda < lambda_ideal stays with Theorem 5.18's human clause, and no fate is decided. In Paper C since the revision of 2026-09-21 (Section 1.4, the Lean paragraph after Corollary 5.5, Appendix A).

Paper C Lemma 4.2 (fiber parity). For m ≥ 10^6 with A_m = (3/2) m^{2/3}, α_m = {A_m}, ε_m = m^{−1/3}, call m good if 22 ε_m ≤ α_m ≤ 1 − 22 ε_m and (α_m ≤ 1/2 − 2 ε_m or α_m ≥ 1/2 + 2 ε_m) — the paper's ‖α_m‖ ≥ 22 m^{−1/3} and ‖α_m − 1/2‖ ≥ 2 m^{−1/3} unpacked (FiberParity.Good). On the OE fiber Φ(m) = {n odd : m⁴ ≤ n³ < (m+1)⁴} (oeFiber) with H_m = |Φ(m)| and G_m = #{n ∈ Φ(m) : Nat.sqrt(n³) even} (evenImageCount): if m is good then G_m ≥ H_m/3 − 2 and H_m − G_m ≥ H_m/3 − 2 (fiber_parity_good). Proof: x(n) = n √n / 2 has ⌊2 x(n)⌋ = Nat.sqrt(n³) (floor_two_xval, Real.floor_real_sqrt_eq_nat_sqrt), so the image is even iff the half-cell of x(n) is even; the step x(n+2) − x(n) = (u² + uv + v²)/(u + v) with u = √(n+2), v = √n (xval_step), lies in [(3/2)v, (3/2)u] by (2u+v)(u−v) ≥ 0 and (u+2v)(u−v) ≥ 0 (xval_step_ge, xval_step_le) and is nondecreasing since the upper bound at n is the lower bound at n+2 (xval_step_mono); the fiber is the odd integers of an interval, enumerated as n₀ + 2j (oeFiber_eq_image), with at least (2/3) m^{1/3} − 1 members (oeFiber_card_ge, Bernoulli on (1+1/m)^{4/3}); along the fiber the steps lie in [A_m, A_m + ε_m] (step_ge, step_le; the upper step at n_{j+1} ∈ Φ(m) gives (3/2)(m+1)^{2/3} ≤ A_m + ε_m by Bernoulli on (1+1/m)^{2/3}). Case 1 (α_m ≤ 1/2 − 2ε_m): y_j = x_j − j⌊A_m⌋ has nondecreasing steps in [α_m, α_m + ε_m], b/a ≤ 21/20 and (H−1)a ≥ 44/3 − 44ε_m ≥ 12, and Sweep.sweep_monotone_cell (row J-fate-monotone-pairing-repair) counts both parities. Case 2 (α_m ≥ 1/2 + 2ε_m): z_j = j(⌊A_m⌋+1) − x_j has nonincreasing steps in [1 − α_m − ε_m, 1 − α_m], (H−1)a ≥ 14 − 42ε_m ≥ 12, and sweep_monotone_ceil counts ⌈2z_j⌉ ≡ ⌊2x_j⌋ (mod 2). Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. The paper's η_m ≤ 1.02 m^{−1/3} becomes ε_m; nothing downstream changes. Lemma 4.3 (bad fibers are thin) stays a human proof; not a statement about all fibers; not a halt theorem.

Paper C Proposition 6.3(i) and the first-letter trichotomy of Section 6.2. If some positive n does not reach 1, the failure set has a least positive member (exists_minimal_failure), and that member is odd with an odd image, i.e. an OO-type start (minimal_failure_odd_odd): an even member n ≥ 2 has the smaller positive member floor(sqrt n) (floorPower_even_lt), and an odd member with even image has the smaller positive member floor(sqrt(floor(n^{3/2}))) < n (floorPower_odd_even_two_step_lt). Stated for any forward-closed class excluding 1 (minimalMember_odd, minimalMember_image_odd). For a two-way closed class A, A n iff exactly one of: n even with J(n) ∈ A; n odd, J(n) even, J(n) ∈ A; n odd, J(n) odd, J(n) ∈ A (first_letter_trichotomy, first_letter_pieces_disjoint) — the three pieces of the identity (6.1). Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. The log-mass bookkeeping of (6.1), the fiber weights and the free term ψ_F are not formalized; not a density theorem, not a halt theorem.

Paper C Theorem 9.2 (pressure form), exact. On the live weight of LiveCountWeight (starts n in {1, …, N} with J^i(n) > N₀ for i ≤ d, liveTo): livePressure N₀ N x d := weightGen (liveWeight N₀ N) x d = Σ_{n live} x^{o_d(n)}; the Markov step live_count_le_pressure gives #{n live, o_d(n) ≥ k} ≤ livePressure / x^k for x ≥ 1 (weight_markov on the live weight, liveCount_sum_oddCount); Lemma 8.1 on live starts: a live n ≤ N has an itinerary that fails the envelope comparison at scale N at every prefix (envelopeBad_of_liveTo, from iterate_le_of_envelope), hence is L(N)-bad with L(N) = log_2(log N / log N₀) (LBad_of_liveTo) and has o_d ≥ p_C d when d ≥ C L(N) (live_oddCount_ge). Theorem: N₀ ≥ 2, N ≥ 2, C ≥ 5, d ≥ 1, d ≥ C L(N), tilt x = p_C/(1 − p_C), a = (1 + x)/2; if livePressure N₀ N x d ≤ N a^d E then #{n ≤ N : liveTo N₀ n d} ≤ N exp(−d D(p_C‖1/2)) E (live_count_le_of_pressure), by a^d / x^{p_C d} = exp(−d D(p_C‖1/2)) (tilt_value); E ≥ 0 is forced since the pressure is a nonnegative sum. This is the exponential-Markov step of Theorem 9.2 with the hypothesis P_θ(C) at one scale and depth in the form pressure ≤ N a_θ^d E; the paper's E = e^{o(d)}, d = ⌈CL⌉ and the displayed (y/2) Λ^{−(e(C)−ε)} are not formalized, and the paper counts odd starts in (y, 2y] where the Lean counts starts in {1, …, N}. Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. Conditional on the pressure bound; nothing here bounds a pressure sum; not a halt theorem.

Paper C Lemma 5.1 (recursion lemma). Let e_i ∈ [e_min, e_max] with 0 < e_min and e_max < 1, c_i real, λ > 0 with ζ := Σ_i c_i e_i^λ - 1 > 0, t_1 > 0, c_0 > 0. Let g : ℝ → ℝ satisfy g(t) ≥ Σ_i (c_i - η_i(t)) g(e_i t) - η_0(t) for all t ≥ t_1, where 0 ≤ η_i(t) ≤ c_i, Σ_i η_i(t) e_i^λ ≤ ζ/3 and η_0(t) ≤ (2ζ/3) c_0 for t ≥ t_1, and g ≥ c_0 on [e_min t_1, t_1]. Then g(t) ≥ c_0 t_1^{-λ} t^λ for all t ≥ e_min t_1 (recursion_lemma). The proof is the paper's induction on N over [e_min t_1, t_1 e_max^{-N}], with exists_pow_lt_of_lt_one supplying N. Weaker hypotheses than the paper's: e_min, e_max are bounds rather than the extrema, λ < 1 and g ≥ 0 are not needed. Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. This is the abstract analytic step of Theorem 5.3; the three-source inequality (5.2) and its constants stay human proofs. The seed (Lemma 5.2) is Lean, row J-fate-seed. Not a density theorem, not a halt theorem.

Paper C Lemma 5.2 (seed). Every nonempty backward-closed A with a positive member contains some m ≥ 3 (exists_ge_three_of_backwardClosed: 1 maps to 2 maps to 4 through even blocks). For any such m and every y ≥ (m+1)^4, the log-mass of A on (√y, y] is at least c_A = (1 − 2/m^4)(3/8 · 1/(m+1) − 1/((m+1)^2 − 1)) (seed_lemma), and c_A > 0 (seed_constant_pos). Proof as in the paper: the even-block tree S_k of m lies in A and in [m^{2^k}, (m+1)^{2^k}); its log-mass grows by at least 1 − 2 m^{-2^k} per level; the product is at least 3/4 by the geometric series 1/(m^2 − 1) ≤ 1/8; at scale k = log2 log_{m+1} y the tree splits at floor(√y) into members above √y, members whose even blocks lie there, and at most one member equal to floor(√y). The integer form y = floor(x) is the paper's g_A(log x). Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. This is one hypothesis of Theorem 5.3; the production inequalities stay human proofs. Not a density theorem, not a halt theorem.

Paper C Lemma 4.1 (sweep). Let x_0 < x_1 < ... < x_{H-1} be reals with consecutive gaps in [a, b], 0 < a ≤ b ≤ 1/2, b ≤ (21/20) a and (H-1) a ≥ 12. Then at least H/7 of the terms have {x_j} < 1/2 and at least H/7 have {x_j} ≥ 1/2 (sweep_fract_lt_half, sweep_fract_ge_half); with the left-open half-cells (k/2, (k+1)/2], i.e. the representative x - ceil(x) + 1 in (0, 1], at least H/7 have representative ≤ 1/2 and at least H/7 have representative > 1/2 (sweep_rep_le_half, sweep_rep_gt_half). Both are instances of sweep_cell: each residue class of the half-cell index floor(2x_j) mod 2 holds at least H/7 terms. Proof as in the paper with one simplification: every cell holds at most G = floor(1/(2a)) + 1 terms (fiber_card_le), every strictly interior cell at least g = floor(1/(2b)) (fiber_card_ge), the number of visited cells T is at least 25 (cell_span), one colour has at least (T-3)/2 interior cells (colour_cells_ge, via Int.Ico_filter_modEq_card), and 3g ≥ G (three_g_ge, the paper's case analysis on X = 1/(2a)); the integer chain 42 Good ≥ 21 g (T-3) ≥ 7 G (T-3) ≥ 6 G T ≥ 6 H closes. The left-open variant is the closed one applied to j ↦ -x_{H-1-j} (Finset.sum_range_reflect). Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. Lemma 4.1' (monotone pairing, H/3 - 2) is not formalized. Not a parity theorem about the Juggler map; the fiber inputs (Lemma 4.2) stay human proofs.

Paper C Theorem 7.3 (the almost-all equivalence), with the contagion bound of Theorem 5.3 as a hypothesis, as for Theorem 7.2 (row J-tao-rate-implies-conjecture). tao_rate_iff_conjecture: for 0 < λ < 1 and the contagion bound K (log x)^λ ≤ logMass (¬ReachesOne) x for x ≥ x₀ whenever the failure set is nonempty, every positive integer reaches 1 iff there is e > 1 − λ and y₀ with #{odd n in (y, 2y] : n does not reach 1} ≤ y (log y)^{−e} for all y ≥ y₀. Paper C Theorem 8.3 (Tao-type bound from the cylinder hypothesis), exact and explicit forms. cylinder y d w is the set of odd n in (y, 2y] with itinerary n d = w; oddFailures y the odd n in (y, 2y] with ¬ReachesOne n; EnvelopeBad N₀ Y w says N₀^{2^t} < Y^{3^{o_t(w)}} for every prefix t ≤ |w|. (i) oddFailures_subset_bad_cylinders: if every start up to N₀ reaches 1, then oddFailures y ⊆ ⋃ {cylinder y d w : w ∈ allWords d, EnvelopeBad N₀ (2y) w} — Lemma 8.1 (reachesOne_of_itinerary_envelope) in covering form, using n ≤ 2y. (ii) oddFailures_card_le: if every envelope-bad cylinder has at most M starts then #oddFailures y ≤ #{envelope-bad words} · M. (iii) LBad_of_envelopeBad: for N₀, Y ≥ 2, envelope-bad at scale Y implies L-bad with L = log_2(log Y / log N₀). (iv) oddFailures_card_le_chernoff: N₀ ≥ 2, y ≥ 1, C ≥ 5, d ≥ 1, d ≥ C L(y) with L(y) = log_2(log 2y / log N₀), M ≥ 0, and every L(y)-bad cylinder of depth d has at most M starts: then #oddFailures y ≤ 2^d · 2^{−e(C) L(y)} · M, by (i)–(iii) and row J-fate-chernoff-count. (v) oddFailures_card_le_explicit: with d = ⌈C L(y)⌉ ≥ 1 (depth), y ≥ 2, and the bound of H(C, A) at the scale y on every O-rooted L(y)-bad cylinder of depth d (E-rooted cylinders are empty, cylinder_even_root_empty), the odd failures in (y, 2y] number at most y Λ^{−e(C)} + 2 Λ^C y (log y)^{−A} with Λ = log 2y / log N₀ (scaleRatio) — at every y, no ε, a factor 2 in the main term against the paper's y/2 Λ^{−(e(C)−ε)}. Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. The paper's displayed form is (v) with the factor 2 absorbed into Λ^ε and the second term into the first for A > C + e(C), not formalized; Corollary 8.4 (the conjecture from a cylinder bound) rests on Theorem 7.2 and stays a human proof. Conditional on the cylinder bound; not a density theorem, not a halt theorem.

Paper C Lemma 4.3 (bad fibers are thin), badness being ¬Good of row J-fate-fiber-parity. (i) bad_count_le: for u ≥ 10^6, #{m ∈ (u, 2u] : ¬Good m} ≤ 63 u^{2/3}. (ii) bad_logMass_le: for U ≥ 10^6 and every N, Σ_{m ∈ (U, N], ¬Good m} 1/m ≤ 306 U^{−1/3} (the paper's infinite sum, as a bound on every partial sum). Proof of (i): the increments of A_m = (3/2) m^{2/3} lie in [(m+1)^{−1/3}, m^{−1/3}] by Bernoulli both ways (Am_step_ge, Am_step_le); a bad m > u has {A_m + 22 u^{−1/3}} < 44 u^{−1/3} or {A_m} ∈ [1/2 − 2u^{−1/3}, 1/2 + 2u^{−1/3}) (bad_mem_arc; the shift makes the wrap-around arc a single arc); arc_count_le: a sequence increasing by at least d per step on (u, v] has at most (⌊φ(v)⌋ − ⌊φ(u+1)⌋ + 1)(w/d + 1) indices with fractional part in an arc [c, c+w) ⊆ [0, 1), by the fibre-per-integer-window count; with d = (2u)^{−1/3} (sharper than the paper's (3u)^{−1/3}), w/d = 44·2^{1/3} and 4·2^{1/3}, the windows number at most A_{2u} − A_u + 2 ≤ 0.882 u^{2/3} + 2 (2^{2/3} ≤ 1.588), and (0.882 u^{2/3} + 2)(48·2^{1/3} + 2) ≤ 63 u^{2/3} for u^{2/3} ≥ 10^4 (2^{1/3} ≤ 1.26). Proof of (ii): on one block (u, 2u] the bad log-mass is at most 63 u^{2/3}/u = 63 u^{−1/3} (bad_block_logMass_le); (U, N] ⊆ (U, 2^N U] which is the disjoint union of the blocks (2^i U, 2^{i+1} U], i < N (bad_sum_dyadic_le); (2^i U)^{−1/3} = (2^{−1/3})^i U^{−1/3} (eps_pow_two_mul); the geometric series gives 63 U^{−1/3}/(1 − 2^{−1/3}) and 2^{−1/3} ≤ 0.794 (0.794^3 ≥ 1/2) gives 63/(1 − 2^{−1/3}) ≤ 306.
